investigations.name: iirabm
investigations.title: Reproducing Cockrell & An (2018): controllability of sepsis in the IIRABM
investigations.description: This investigation reproduces the figures and results of Cockrell RC, An G, "Examining the controllability of sepsis using genetic algorithms on an agent-based model of systemic inflammation," PLoS Comput Biol 14(2):e1005876 (2018). The IIRABM is wrapped as a real-bridge process-bigraph Process (viva_iirabm.IIRABMProcess); every number is produced by the original C++ model. The compute-heavy portions of the paper (GA training and the 8,291-set generalizability sweep) used ~1,000,000 CPU-hours on Cray supercomputers and are reproduced here as METHOD at reduced scale, clearly labeled.
investigations.question: Can the key results of Cockrell & An (2018) — a high-mortality in-silico sepsis regime, genetic-algorithm-identified multi-stage cytokine interventions that lower mortality, the non-responder phenomenon, and partial generalizability of a fixed intervention — be reproduced from the genuine IIRABM C++ simulator?
investigations.hypothesis: Driving the real An & Cockrell IIRABM (wrapped as a process-bigraph Process) reproduces the paper's qualitative and approximate quantitative findings: the trained parameter set kills ~82% of stochastic replicates; a GA over cytokine augmentation/inhibition discovers interventions that shift the population toward survival; some patients are intrinsic "non-responders"; and a single derived intervention helps across a range of parameter sets but not all.
